t.7.95.1: While the two of them were thus conversing, the blessed sage Durvāsā, desiring to see Rāma, came to the gate of the royal palace.
t.7.95.2: Having approached Saumitri, that best of sages said: "Show me Rāma quickly, before my purpose slips away."
t.7.95.3: Having heard the words of the sage, Lakṣmaṇa, slayer of enemy heroes, saluted the great-souled one and spoke these words.
t.7.95.4: Tell me, blessed one, what is the task, or what is your purpose? What shall I do? For Rāghava is occupied, O brahman; let your honor wait a moment.
t.7.95.5: Hearing that, the tiger among sages, clouded with anger, spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa, as if burning him up with his eyes.
t.7.95.6: This very moment, O Saumitri, announce me to Rāma; otherwise I shall curse the kingdom, you, the city, and Rāghava as well.
t.7.95.8: Having heard that terrible-seeming speech of the great-souled one, he pondered in his mind the certain meaning of those words.
t.7.95.7: Bharata too, O Saumitri, and whatever offspring you all have; for I shall no longer be able to hold back the anger in my heart.
t.7.95.10: Having heard Lakṣmaṇa's words, Rāma dismissed Kāla, and the king, hastening out, beheld the son of Atri.
t.7.95.9: "Let death come to me alone; let there not be the destruction of all." Having firmly resolved thus in his mind, he announced the matter to Rāghava.
t.7.95.11: Having saluted the great-souled one, who seemed to blaze with splendor, Kākutstha, with joined palms, said: "What is to be done?"
t.7.95.12: Having heard those words spoken by Rāghava, the mighty Durvāsas, foremost among sages, replied to Rāma: "Listen, O you who cherish dharma."
t.7.95.13: Today, O Rāghava, my thousand years come to completion. So I desire food, O sinless one, whatever you have ready.
t.7.95.14: Hearing those words, Rāma, filled with great joy, brought food, just as it had been prepared, to the foremost of sages.
t.7.95.15: Having eaten that nectar-like food, the best of sages said, "Well done, Rāma!" and went back to his own hermitage.
t.7.95.16: When he had gone, the greatly radiant Rāghava, though glad at heart, then recalled the words of Kāla and was overcome with sorrow.
t.7.95.17: Sorely tormented by grief, and remembering that dreadful sight, he stood with his face cast down and his heart desolate, and could not utter a word.
t.7.95.18: Then Rāghava, having weighed the words of Kāla with his understanding, said, "This is not so," and the greatly renowned one fell silent.
